Conflicts: birds⟷bats, fireflies⟷pollen; water/thunder/sandstorm/leaves compatible with everything. Demo button (Settings) ONLY changes the effect (AUTO/NONE/each effect); AUTO prints the live active effect. NEW 2026-09-07: moths/ — the LAMP DANCE, the first of the maintainer's new effect list. A few cream specks hold a squashed elliptical orbit (the iso plane is shallow) round a lit lamp and DIVE at it now and then; night only, outdoors, unsealed lamps of radius >= 1.5 only. Lamps come from a second read-only seam on WorldScene, __ml.lightsInView(pad) — every EmissiveSource the camera sees (emissive tiles AND scenery lamps) as {id, x, y, r, color, sealed}. IT MUST NOT COST A FRAME (maintainer): the lamp list is read on a 520 ms THROTTLE (it walks every source in the world), per-frame work is trig on at most 10 pooled sprites, and a DAY frame returns before any of it. __mlAmbient.cost(reset?) now times every feature's own update — measured moths 0.027 ms/frame at night, 0.018 by day, both at the timer's noise floor. NEW 2026-09-07 (2): moths now circle the LIGHT, not the foot of the post — a light record's sx/sy is its ANCHOR and its z the emissive head's lift above it (0.3-1.5 levels, measured off the lit art), so lightsInView returns y already lifted to the head, with footY and z alongside; the head sits 22.5px above the post on the town's street lamp. AND gnats/ — the COLUMN that hangs over one spot at dusk: a couple of dozen specks flying hard inside a narrow vertical volume that stands still (anchor moves 0px, swarm within 8.6px of its axis), Evening full / Morning half, gone in rain, storm, snow or wind; walk into it and it breaks up in 220ms and gathers again over 1.4s. 0.034 ms/frame at dusk, 0.011 by day. NEW 2026-09-07 (3): crabs/ — the SIDEWAYS SCUTTLE at the water's edge. Four-pixel crabs on sand beside water: still, then a short hard run ALONG the shore, and the whole beach moving at once when the player comes near. The shore axis is DERIVED — the search that finds the beach records which way the water lies and the run axis is its perpendicular, so crabs run along any coast at any angle with no per-map data. Measured: 255 of 255 runs on the axis, 1540 samples all on land and none on water, colony on real sand with water 48px away. TOGGLEABLE: the gate opens the Settings page, finds the row by the LABEL A PLAYER READS, clicks it like a player, and requires the effect to start and stop drawing - testing the API underneath would not catch a missing row, and a missing row is what he would see. FPS: three numbers, because 'it feels fine' is not a measurement - the feature's own ms/frame (0.032 on a beach), its probe rate (9.7/s), and THE INLAND WORST CASE, standing where no beach exists so the search can never succeed (0.013 ms/frame, 0.64 searches/s against a naive version's one per frame). The pattern for every effect that has to FIND something: rate-limit the search itself, not just its success.

[2026-09-07T21:07:47+00:00] BUBBLES + the crab correction. Crabs shipped neither red nor bigger than a spider (4x2 burnt orange beside a 3x3 spider) - the maintainer caught both on sight, and neither is visible to a test that only checks positions, so the gate now compares the two features' PUBLISHED art sizes (the spider publishes its own) and checks the drawn tint is red-dominant. For bubbles his standing fade rule is measured PER BUBBLE, tracked by id across frames: a snapshot cannot tell an arriving bubble from a leaving one, and 'nothing pops out of existence' is exactly a per-object property. 135 of 139 arrived faint, 136 of 139 left faint. THE PATTERN FOR EVERY 'find a place' EFFECT is now settled: rate-limit the SEARCH, not just its success, and gate the worst case where it can never succeed - crabs inland 0.66 searches/s, bubbles inland 0.83 hunts/s and zero vents.

[2026-09-08T07:49:32+00:00] 'THEY BOTH NEED MORE SPACE' - the maintainer liked both effects and both were sized like decorations. Two general lessons. (1) A SNAPPED DIRECTION IS NOT A GRADIENT: the crab shore axis came from the first of eight sample offsets that hit water, so it could be 22 degrees off the real coast and a straight walk along it left the sand after two steps - 78px of 'beach', one tile, which was exactly his complaint. Averaging a ring of hits gives a real gradient, and walking with a turn at each step follows a curve. (2) A LOCAL RULE MUST STAY LOCAL WHEN THE THING GROWS: 'the whole beach reacts at once' was one distance test from the colony's centre, which was fine at one tile and became 'the entire 480px beach panics whenever you are near it' - now per crab, which is both truer and what he liked ('it was cool that they tried to dodge me'). Both gates needed the same treatment: a fixed pixel tolerance silently tightens as the thing it measures grows.

[2026-09-08T11:26:49+00:00] Round two on both. CRABS: a transition tile is ONE CELL whose art is part sand and part water, so every per-cell probe says 'landable' for a point the player sees as sea - the boundary is in the artwork and cannot be asked about. Measured instead: each shoreline point finds its own first WATER CELL and a crab stands 22px back from it (half a tile diamond bounds the wet part). Edges smoothed, or the crab jinks in and out on the 6px quantisation - 53 of 562 runs off the shore tangent before, 1 of 528 after. GNATS: 'more spread out, denser in the middle' is a MIXTURE, not a wider curve - every curve with a fatter tail drags its median out too, so the core spreads with the rim. Most gnats come from a tight core, 22% are wanderers over the whole reach, and the wanderers are dimmer in proportion to their reach. AND THE BREATHING SWING IS LOAD-BEARING: a radius swinging 0.4-1.0 of a gnat's reach means it is only ever SEEN wide when two sines peak together, so raising the column radius 40 -> 70 moved the widest gnat observed from 36px to 41. Narrow the swing and it goes where it belongs.

[2026-09-08T13:24:49+00:00] GNATS, round three, and the general lesson: A DISTRIBUTION'S TAIL IS NOT ITS SILHOUETTE. Reading 'denser in the middle' as a tight core plus a few far wanderers made the swarm NARROWER to the eye while every measurement said it had grown - the widest gnat reached 42px, but that was one rare individual and the BULK sat at 6px, which is what a person reads as the size. Fixed by sizing off his own screenshot (calibrated against CHARACTER_BODY_PX: his circle is ~130 wu across and 118 tall, so a cloud about as wide as it is tall, spanning two tiles) and by gating the NINETIETH PERCENTILE rather than the maximum. Any future 'make it bigger' request on a scattered effect should be gated on a percentile of the bulk, never on an extreme.

[2026-09-08T17:00:23+00:00] MOTHS, round three, and the answer to 'do we need new scenery data' is NO - the game already measures it and was throwing it away. A lit piece's glowing centroid is derived from its own pixels (headY, WorldScene) and then CLAMPED to 1.5 levels for the light pool, because a head four levels up leaves the ground under a streetlight near the pool's edge. That clamp is correct for LIGHTING and wrong for DRAWING: every tall lamp reports its flame at 22.5px, which is down on the post, and the town lamp's real lift is 61.6px (4.1 levels). The unclamped point now travels on the record as hx/hy beside the clamped z - both right for their own job. The seam also publishes `flicker`, which is how the game already distinguishes a FIRE from a steady lamp, so ember sparks can ask rather than guess from an id. NOTHING IS NEEDED FROM THE SCENERY AGENT.

GATE LESSON, twice paid: a spiral of teleports cannot find a thing 53 cells away on a 12-angle ring with a 7-cell view, so the targets are DERIVED from the world doc and the piece manifests the game itself reads; and a search that moves the player must put them back, or the measurement runs somewhere else.

[2026-09-08T18:53:47+00:00] A SOURCE-ATTACHED EFFECT FOLLOWS ITS SOURCE, NOT THE ROOF — a charter refinement, paid for immediately. Embers inherited the outdoor rule (every feature multiplies by ctx.outdoor, because rain and birds fall through a cut-away roof) and was therefore silently dead beside the most atmospheric fire in the game: the maintainer stood next to a cave brazier with the switch on and saw nothing. Measured at his spot 256,167: outdoor gain 0, so the feature returned before reading anything. Most ember placements on the_game are indoors, so that was the common case. Now: an unsealed source works wherever you are, a sealed one only while you are indoors (when its roof is cut away) — without that second half the sparks would draw over the roof hiding their own fire, which is the wall-hack the cut-away exists to prevent. Effects that fill the AIR keep the plain outdoor rule.

[2026-09-08T22:43:36+00:00] A COUNTER CANNOT SEE THE SCREEN — the ember sparks shipped INVISIBLE and every check I had passed. The sprites were setOrigin(0.5,0.5) on a 1x1 texture, and a one-pixel quad centred on an integer position straddles two pixels, so the renderer drops it: measured, a spark on screen at alpha 0.81 moved its pixel by 0.1 luma. The feature's own numbers were all correct and all irrelevant (visible, right depth, right alpha, right position, texture present). Every other pixel mark in ambient/ uses origin (0,0) and that is why they can be seen. Fixed, same spark now moves its pixel by 54 luma, and verify-embers gained a PIXEL arm — centre the camera on the fire, find the brightest spark in frame, require the pixel under it to change when the effect is switched off. Any future ambient effect gets that arm; three rounds of 'I can't see a single spark' is what a counters-only gate costs.

[2026-09-09T01:33:14+00:00] TECHNICALLY VISIBLE IS NOT VISIBLE. The embers took three 'I can't see a single spark' reports and two distinct bugs, both invisible to counters. (1) setOrigin(0.5,0.5) on a 1x1 texture: a one-pixel quad centred on an integer straddles two pixels and the renderer drops it — a spark at alpha 0.81 moved its pixel by 0.1 luma. Every other pixel mark in ambient/ uses origin (0,0). (2) ONE WORLD PIXEL IS ABOUT ONE CSS PIXEL on his phone (zoom 3 against dpr 2.75), so even correctly drawn it could not be found over a lit fireplace; a spark is now 2x2 while hot, shrinking to 1x1 as it dies, and leaves the flame WHITE-HOT before cooling to the fire's colour. MEASURING IT WAS THE HARD PART and the lesson is general: a hearth's art is ANIMATED, so a single off-frame baseline reports the flame (195 luma with the effect OFF); the arm now builds a PER-PIXEL MAX ENVELOPE over eight off frames and requires the spark to beat the fire at its brightest in every phase — 47.5 luma against a 0.6 control. Every future ambient effect gets a pixel arm built this way.

requests.text: Heads up: I edited one of your files, games2/server/test/noaggro.test.ts, to unblock deploys — sorry for crossing the line, it was one digit and it was stopping everyone. It picked port 2993, which timeofday.test.ts already uses; I moved it to 2990. node:test runs each test FILE in its own process and several of them CONCURRENTLY, so the two raced to bind 2993 and the loser waited forever. That is why main had not gone live since 8aeda9c34: the CI test job ran 3 HOURS before GitHub killed it (no failure, no output, it just stopped) and the deploy job died with 'timed out waiting for the test job'. It never reproduces for anyone running the suite sequentially — --test-concurrency=1 passes in 68s every time. Parallel was hanging indefinitely; it is now 24-26s. I also added games2/server/test/ports.test.ts, which fails the build when two test files claim the same port and names both — the files already said 'unique per test file', what was missing was something that checks. If you add a test that listens, either pick a port no other file uses or bind port 0 and read it back the way live.test.ts does. Also FYI I regenerated npcs.json (stale idleAnim: null after the characters2 sync) but characters2 landed the same fix first, so my commit dropped out on rebase.

I added one probe to your WorldScene: __ml.deepCurrentAtScreen(wx, wy) — screen coords in like waterAtScreen, out is the shared deepCurrentAt reading (flat world unit vector toward the map centre + wu/s, or null on land/lakes/free shallows). Four lines, read-only, next to waterAtScreen/landableAtScreen, over a function WorldScene already imports and calls for prediction. Sorry for reaching into your file — ambient had no way to do this itself: water and deep_water carry IDENTICAL Surface records (swimmable, speed 0.55, sound water), so waterAtScreen, surfaceAt and gridAround all answer the same for a pond and for the end of the world, and t3at is a heavyweight debug probe. The maintainer asked for a deep_water-specific effect that visualises the current dragging you back, so the distinction had to exist somewhere. It is now ambient/deepwater/ — swells rolling inward with foam over them, streaming along YOUR vector at YOUR speed, so the sea carries the player back at the rate it actually does. Two things you may want: (1) I found nothing wrong with timeOfDay, but note __ml.timeSpeed takes a NUMBER — passing {v:0} silently no-ops, which cost me an hour of chasing a phantom inverted day/night gate; a guard or a doc line there would save the next agent. (2) main's CI is red — 20 failures across world3, tiles3, scenery3, tiles3draw and spawns3 (stale fixtures + a ground with no SURFACES entry). Not mine and I have not touched them, but worth knowing that the deploy's own test job passed at a commit where CI failed, so the two gates are disagreeing and main can deploy while CI is red.

Second probe added to your WorldScene, same shape as deepCurrentAtScreen: __ml.lightsInView(pad = 96) — every EmissiveSource whose drawn anchor lands in a padded worldView, from BOTH this.emissiveSources and this.sceneryLightSources, as {id, x, y, r, color, sealed}. Read-only, no allocation beyond the returned array, sitting right before lightSlots. Ambient had no way to derive it: a lamp's DRAWN anchor (sx, sy) and its sealed-in-a-room verdict exist only inside those arrays, and lightSlots reports the 8 SLOTTED lights rather than what is in view — a street with more lamps than slots would have gone dark for us. It is for ambient/moths/, the maintainer's 'moths circling a lamp'. Note for anyone else who calls it: it walks every source in the world, so it wants a throttle — moths reads it about twice a second and does nothing but trig in between, measured 0.027 ms/frame. Related: __mlAmbient.cost() now reports each ambient feature's own update in ms/frame, so 'is ambient what is lagging' has an answer that does not depend on frame-time noise.

Two fields added to EmissiveSource in your WorldScene, both additive and neither read by the lighting: hx/hy, the DRAWN position of a source's glowing centroid, unclamped. You already compute it as headY in pushSceneryLight and then clamp it into `z` at 1.5 levels for the pool — which is right for lighting and was silently wrong for anything that has to draw AT the flame: the town's street lamp reports 1.5 levels (22.5px) against a real 61.6px, so ambient's moths circled the middle of the post twice in a row and the maintainer photographed it both times. `z` is untouched; hx/hy sit beside it, and __ml.lightsInView now returns the drawn point plus `flicker` (fire vs steady lamp). If you ever want the same for the wiki's shadow/light editors, the number is now on the record rather than derived twice.

REQUEST (maintainer-approved 2026-09-08): publish a light TYPE, so a consumer can tell what a light IS. WHERE: the existing `light` block in scenery/<group>/<piece>/scenery.json, beside strength/color/radius, and overridable per state exactly as those three already are — brazier_001's LIT_1 is cyan (#4bffde) and its LIT_2 amber (#ffb45c), so one piece can plausibly be two kinds of light and the per-state override is not hypothetical. WHY IT CANNOT BE DERIVED, all four checked: the block has no type; `tags` is ["SCENERY"] on every piece; the game's own `flicker` is a BRIGHTNESS decision, not a semantic one (lightKindOf matches /light|lamp|lantern|torch|brazier|fire|candle|beacon|hearth|forge/, so a street lamp is 'flame' to it); and colour classifies nothing — the_game ships torch_post_004 as a blue resin flame (#b4d7ff) while plenty of cold glows are warm amber. Classifying by piece GROUP works and is written, but it is a hardcoded guess living in the game rather than data living with the art, which is why the maintainer would rather you published it. SUGGESTED VOCABULARY (yours and his to name — the shape matters more than the words): `fire` something is burning with an open flame (campfire, brazier, hearth, forge, torch_post, cauldron_camp, charcoal_kiln); `lamp` a made, contained, steady light (streetlight, lantern_post, lantern_stand); `magic` an arcane glow (crystal, soulstone_outcrop, waystone, some shrines); `fungal` a living glow (giant_mushroom, mushroom, toadstool_ring, crystal_tree?). SIZE: 499 of 706 pieces publish a light that lights, across 105 groups. If you want a priority order, the 17 groups that light the SHIPPED map (the_game) are, by placement count: crystals 27, streetlights 23, cauldron_camps 16, wayside_shrines 12, toadstool_rings 11, crystal_trees 8, giant_mushrooms 8, lantern_posts 7, braziers 7, mushrooms 7, charcoal_kilns 7, soulstone_outcrops 3, torch_posts 2, waystones 2, hearths 1, beacons 1, ancient_trees 1. THREE NEED HIS TASTE, not ours: wayside_shrines (votive flame or magic?), beacons (a beacon fire, or a magic light?), crystal_trees (fungal or magic?). WHO CONSUMES IT: ambient/embers — ember sparks rising off a fire — is written and PARKED unregistered until this exists; it needs `fire` and nothing else. WHERE the light is was already solved without you: the game derives a piece's glowing centroid from its own pixels, so no anchor data is needed.

Not a request, a measurement, in case it saves you time on the tiles2 retirement: the deploy pipeline has been down since dc23b51893. `npm test`'s server suite no longer terminates — run 3279 ran it for 20 minutes before GitHub killed the job, and every run since (3280 wiki, 3281 ambient) has had build-deploy fail at 'Wait for the test gate' with 'Deploy to Cloud Run' SKIPPED, so nothing has reached production since 995cb61148. Reproduced locally on the current tip: the suite was still going past 15 minutes and the last thing it printed was WorldRoom's `[staging] world "monster_demo"` line — a world the retirement deleted, so readWorldDoc misses on disk and goes to the network for it. 19 files under server/test/ still name a retired world (monster_demo, house_demo, occlusion_test, the_island2, glow_test, trans_demo, prop_demo, ring_test, demo_isle, demo_lost), and 16 assertions fail before the run even reaches the hang. One more thing that will bite after the tests are green: the deploy workflow's test job sparse-checks-out `/maps2/worlds/`, which no longer exists, and does NOT check out `/maps2/worlds3/` — so CI would run the suite with no world data at all even once it passes. games2/CLAUDE.md already flags that gap ('THE DEPLOY GATE AND CI MUST SEE THE SAME WORLD'); the retirement turns it from partial into total. I have touched none of it — it is yours and you are mid-flight.
